newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore port faces rising competition - minister.
newsitem.headline: Singapore port faces rising competition - minister.

text.p: The Port of Singapore will face rising competition in southeast Asia over the next 20 years, but it should remain a major hub in the region, Minister of Communications Mah Bow Tan said on Tuesday.

Mah was speaking to reporters after a ceremony marking the the Port of Singapore Authority's (PSA) completion of two new berths costing Singapore $600 million (US$426 million) for a new container terminal.
"We cannot realistically be the only hub port in this region for the next 20 years but we can, realistically, be one of the major ports providing very good service for our customers," he said.
"We will continue to position Singapore as a major hub port in the region."
He said container throughput in the region was expected to double by the year 2000 to around 120 million twenty-foot equivalent (TEU).
"There is plenty of business to go around", he said.
"As the business grows, there will be room for another one if not more major ports in the region," he told reporters.
Mah said Singapore regarded competition as both a threat and an opportunity.
A threat because there would be some diversion of cargoes, but an opportunity because, as more ports are developed, extra business would arise, Mah said.
To stay competitive and retain if not improve its share of the market, Singapore aimed to improve productivity, and invest in infrastructure and training, Mah said.
PSA is expected to add two more berths by 1998 to the new container terminal and the four berths will have total capacity of 2.5 million to three million TEU.
The new terminal will eventually have a total of 26 container berths and will cost more than S$7 billion.
Mah also said the PSA will continue to seek agreements with shipping consortia and individual shipping lines to improve business.
